refresh_policy.rationale: ChatGPT requires owner-authenticated browser state. Automatic refresh is session-reuse-only; owner-mediated repair handles provider login challenges through runtime assistance evidence.

display.label: Your conversations
display.detail: Conversation list with titles, create/update times, archived/starred flags, workspace (if enterprise), current-branch tip. Messages are a separate stream.

streams.name: messages
streams.description: Messages within conversations, flattened from ChatGPT's tree structure to the current-branch path. When filtering removes intermediate nodes, parent_id links to the nearest retained ancestor. The filtered message count is reported through PROGRESS.

display.label: Your messages
display.detail: Each message on the current branch of every conversation: role, content, model, create time, tool calls, citations, attachment IDs. Alt branches are not exported. When filtering removes intermediate nodes, parent_id links to the nearest retained ancestor; the filtered count is reported through PROGRESS.

id.description: Record id: the conversation id and the source node id joined by ":" ("<conversation_id>:<node_id>"). ChatGPT copies message nodes into forked conversations, so a node id can recur across conversations and does not identify a message by itself. Versions before 0.3.0 used the bare node id here; node_id carries that value now.

node_id.description: The source's node id for this message, unique within its conversation. conversations.current_node is a node id.

parent_id.description: Record id (the id of another messages record in this conversation) of the nearest retained ancestor, or null for the root. May name a record that was not emitted when the ancestor is the source's synthetic root.

children_ids.description: Record ids of the source node's children, including children on other branches that are not emitted.

content.description: Full message text in the pdpp-safe-escape-v1 encoding. For text and multimodal_text bodies it is the string entries of the source parts joined with a newline, as the legacy collector joins them; the other entries are in non_string_parts. Each code unit in U+0000-0008, U+000B, U+000C, U+000E-001F, U+007F-009F or a lone surrogate (U+D800-DFFF not part of a valid pair) is written as a six-character \uXXXX escape with uppercase hex. A source backslash that starts a \uXXXX whose code unit is in that set or is U+005C is written \u005C. All other text, including noncharacters and valid surrogate pairs, is unchanged. To decode, replace each \uXXXX whose code unit is U+005C or in the escaped set with that code unit. Text whose escaped form exceeds 1048576 characters is not truncated: content is null and blob_ref holds the full text. When the text cannot be stored (the host has no blob store, or its JSON encoding exceeds 33554432 bytes) content and blob_ref are both absent from the record; the run reports a message_content_omitted diagnostic count.

non_string_parts.description: For text and multimodal_text bodies, the entries of the source parts array that are not strings (asset pointers with their size and generation metadata, audio transcripts, any other object), each { index, part } with index the position in parts. content joins only the string parts. Every string inside every entry, at any depth and including object keys, is in the pdpp-safe-escape-v1 encoding (decode it as content is decoded). Empty for other content types.

tool_calls.description: Tool calls. Every string inside every entry, at any depth and including object keys, is in the pdpp-safe-escape-v1 encoding (decode it as content is decoded). An entry that carries a message body may use text_ref "content" in place of text when the message content is blob-backed (blob_ref) or omitted: the body is the content field.

blob_ref.description: Present only when content is null because the text is over the inline cap. The blob (application/json) is the JSON string of the exact source text, with no pdpp-safe-escape-v1 escaping: JSON.parse(bytes) returns the source text for the content field.

streams.name: memories
streams.description: Saved memories ChatGPT has about the user.

display.label: ChatGPT memories
display.detail: Saved facts ChatGPT remembers about you, with created/updated timestamps. Deletions detected via diff — API does not emit tombstones.

streams.name: custom_gpts
streams.description: Custom GPTs (gizmos) the user has authored via the GPT builder.

display.label: Your custom GPTs
display.detail: Custom GPTs you built: name, description, system instructions, enabled tools (code_interpreter, browse, dalle), welcome message, author, visibility, and share URL slug.

streams.name: custom_instructions
streams.description: The user's custom instructions (the 'What would you like ChatGPT to know about you' and 'How would you like ChatGPT to respond' fields).

display.label: Your custom instructions
display.detail: The two free-text fields from Settings → Personalization → Custom Instructions: 'about you' context and preferred response style, plus whether they're currently enabled. Singleton — only one set per user.

streams.name: shared_conversations
streams.description: Conversations the user has shared via public link.

display.label: Your shared conversations
display.detail: Share records for conversations you've made public: the share ID, the underlying conversation, the public URL, anonymous flag, and any highlighted text.

streams.name: account_plan
streams.description: The subscription plan of the signed-in ChatGPT account, with its renewal, expiry and cancellation dates and any scheduled plan change.

display.label: Your ChatGPT plan
display.detail: Which plan the signed-in account is on (free, Plus, Pro, Team…), whether the subscription is active and set to renew, its billing period, the renewal/expiry/cancellation dates, any scheduled plan change, and when the account was created. Usage limits are not included. Payment details and billing identifiers are not collected. Singleton — one record for the account the session is signed in to.

profiles.label: Everything: chats, memories, custom GPTs, custom instructions, shares, account plan

pageshim.exception: Preserves the mobile ChatGPT result envelope while applying list-window filtering.

reason_display_messages.branch_tip_missing: A conversation points at a message we couldn't find, so part of it is missing
reason_display_messages.branch_truncated: A conversation is missing earlier messages from its current thread
reason_display_messages.conversation_list_unstable: ChatGPT's conversation list changed between checks, so try again
reason_display_messages.empty_detail: We opened this conversation but found no messages to import
reason_display_messages.http_error: We hit a network problem talking to the service
reason_display_messages.missing_mapping: We opened this conversation but it had no message data to read
reason_display_messages.not_available: This data isn't available through the current connection
reason_display_messages.pagination_cap_truncated: There were more ChatGPT results than we could safely page through in one run, so we stopped early
reason_display_messages.parse_error: ChatGPT sent back a response we couldn't read
reason_display_messages.shape_check_failed: The data didn't look like we expected
